prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant produces compliant potable water; boundary River Intake Pump Station (Ironwood)–High Service Pump Header; distribution excluded. Ironwood: automatic/withdrawal-limited; readiness/interlocks govern starts; faults inhibit/stop/alarm. Chief Operator authorizes manual/Storm Intake Mode and stable recovery; storm requires increased sampling/discretionary-work re-review.
Raw Water Screen Channel sends Rake Torque Snapshot to Maintenance Planner (Quarry); high-high needs field confirmation. Coagulant Dosing Skid (Marigold) sends Alum Batch Ticket; Laboratory Technician verifies identity; Chief Operator confirms dose; Duty Engineer approves rapid-turbidity changes. Feedback loss requires safe fixed dosing/grabs; coagulation failure requires feed/mixing/basin assessment.
North Filter Gallery (Cobalt) records turbidity/headloss; South Filter Gallery sends Filter Run Exception Note; return requires rinse-to-waste/stability. Backwash Recovery Tank returns require sampling. Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench (Sparrow) receives custody-controlled samples/sends checked Jar Test Photograph Set; Laboratory Technician sends Sample Chain Slip, confirms maintenance sampling/acceptance concerns/residuals. Invalid samples: troubleshooting-only; release requires quality-control review. SCADA Historian Server (Lantern) retains synchronized results/operating data/pre/post-work comparisons.
Chlorine Contact Basin must maintain required contact time for production/level/residual; adjust chlorine gradually. Chlorine Residual Alarm requires assessment/priority grabs, analyzer-flow verification/grab comparison, production-increase hold; maintenance pauses pending operations’ cause confirmation.
Clearwell Level Controller protects contact/reserve/suction; low-level interlocks prevent unsafe pumping; high alarms permit production/pumping adjustment.
Work orders require approvals/isolations/craft verification/operations acknowledgment, capacity protection, return evidence/acceptance, temporary-item removal/formal acceptance. Failed tests keep orders open; Chief Operator determines isolation/restrictions and confirms chlorine controls/residual instruments/levels consistent in Lantern before normal disinfection. Turnover includes restrictions/abnormalities.
Chemical Supplier Driver sends Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log before approved/operator-observed unloading; inspect hoses/containment/washdown. Basin work requires ventilation/gas monitoring/communications. Distribution Dispatcher receives advance maintenance-impact notice for header/North Distribution Pressure Station/South Distribution Pressure Station. Residuals Hauler removes residuals/backwash.

New part:
S134: The Clearwell Level Controller sends the Clearwell Diver Entry Permit when level and isolation prerequisites have been verified by the control system.
S135: Clearwell level changes are trended against filter production and high-service demand so that slow instrumentation errors can be distinguished from actual storage changes.
S136: The High Service Pump Header is identified in voice radio traffic by the alias Juniper when operators need a short confirmation name.
S137: The High Service Pump Header sequences available pumps to meet distribution demand while avoiding unnecessary starts, short cycling, and operation near unstable portions of the pump curves.
S138: Lead and lag pump assignments are rotated according to runtime, availability, and any operating restriction entered by the Chief Operator.
S139: Header pressure control uses a paced response so that pump starts, pump speed changes, and valve movements do not create avoidable pressure transients in the distribution system.
S140: The High Service Pump Header produces the Pump Bearing Vibration Clip after a configured vibration threshold is exceeded during pump operation.
S141: If a high-service pump trips, the remaining available pumps are evaluated automatically against the current pressure setpoint before another unit is started.
S142: The North Distribution Pressure Station and South Distribution Pressure Station receive pressure support through coordinated setpoints that reflect system demand and storage conditions.
S143: The Distribution Dispatcher is identified by the alias Falcon during pressure coordination calls with plant staff.
S144: The Distribution Dispatcher communicates expected demand changes, main break impacts, and pressure complaints so that plant pumping decisions match field conditions.
S145: During Storm Intake Mode, operators watch the relationship between raw water quality, filter loading, disinfectant demand, and high-service pumping to avoid forcing production beyond treatment capability.
S146: Abnormal clearwell level, loss of residual, loss of pump header pressure, or conflicting instrument readings require the Duty Engineer to review the operating condition before setpoints are changed outside normal ranges.
S147: The SCADA Historian Server stores residual, level, pressure, and pump status data at sufficient resolution to support event reconstruction after alarms or customer pressure complaints.
S148: Manual operation is allowed only when the operator can maintain residual targets, clearwell limits, and distribution pressure with direct observation of the affected indications.
S149: Return to automatic control requires stable chlorine residual, stable clearwell level response, and confirmed high-service pressure control for a period set by the Chief Operator.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
